methodology.date: measured during development, real Chrome 131 (headless), Puppeteer
methodology.hardware: 1 vCPU container, no GPU, WASM-only execution (WebGPU confirmed unavailable in this environment - see docs/LIMITATIONS.md items 19 and 20)
methodology.page: a procedurally generated 'realistic' synthetic page: nav with 20 links, 60 status-card divs, a login form (username/password/email/phone), a 30x6 data table, 4 canvas elements - 387 total extracted DOM elements
methodology.protocol: 1 untimed warm-up run (model init + JIT warm-up), then 10 timed iterations, statistics computed over the 10 timed runs only
methodology.note: This is a real measurement with a real, disclosed methodology - NOT a claim about typical end-user hardware. A real user's machine has more CPU cores, likely a working GPU (enabling the WebGPU fast path this container cannot exercise at all), and a browser cache already warmed by prior page loads. Treat these numbers as a conservative (worse-case) reference point, not a performance guarantee.

interpretation: Isolating the two conditions shows the real cost driver clearly: DOM-only perception on a 387-element realistic page is fast (~14ms median total). Adding 4 canvas elements that trigger real OCR + face-detection + scene-classification inference raises total per-cycle latency to ~140ms median, ~232ms p95 - the image/vision scan step alone accounts for ~95% of that increase. This scales with the NUMBER of images/canvases on a page, not the number of ordinary DOM elements, which is the expected and correct behavior given the architecture (see docs/MODEL_PIPELINE.md).
